The tape layout arranges the address bits so that each round of a [synthetic polynomial transform](synthetic-transform.md) runs as one [simultaneous butterfly layer](simultaneous-layer.md) instead of one pass per axis.
This needs at most $Dq-1$ exchanges, each made by the [fast address-chunk interchange](address-interchange.md) at cost $O(TpK^\tau)$, even for nonadjacent chunks

Outputs keep the bit-reversed order of [retained frequency order](frequency-order.md), written $B$ along every axis (the bit-reversal permutation here, not the row length of the stream-operations page or the suffix digit count of the controlled-shifts page).

symbols.name: transformed axis count
symbols.meaning: The number of transformed axes, d-1.
symbols.quote: Write $\ell=\log_2 r$, the address bits of a long axis (an address-bit count, not the depth of a value), and $D=d-1$, the number of transformed axes (not the second chunk value of the address-interchange page, the source group of the matrix-shear page, or the selected chunk count of the simultaneous-layer page).

symbols.name: leftover low bits
symbols.meaning: The number of leftover low bits of an axis.
symbols.quote: Put $b=(\ell-1)\bmod K$, the number of leftover low bits of an axis (not the lowest output-index bit of the butterfly page, a digit count of the matrix-shear or controlled-shifts pages, or a kernel coefficient), and $q=\lfloor(\ell-1)/K\rfloor$, its number of whole chunks (not a sequence length of the DFT and convolution pages, nor a radix or prime), so $\ell-1=qK+b$.

symbols.name: whole chunks
symbols.meaning: The number of whole K-bit chunks of an axis.
symbols.quote: Put $b=(\ell-1)\bmod K$, the number of leftover low bits of an axis (not the lowest output-index bit of the butterfly page, a digit count of the matrix-shear or controlled-shifts pages, or a kernel coefficient), and $q=\lfloor(\ell-1)/K\rfloor$, its number of whole chunks (not a sequence length of the DFT and convolution pages, nor a radix or prime), so $\ell-1=qK+b$.

symbols.name: bit reversal
symbols.meaning: The bit-reversal permutation applied along every axis.
symbols.quote: Outputs keep the bit-reversed order of [retained frequency order](frequency-order.md), written $B$ along every axis (the bit-reversal permutation here, not the row length of the stream-operations page or the suffix digit count of the controlled-shifts page).

symbols.name: layout permutation
symbols.meaning: The record permutation defined by the prefix moves and chunk exchanges.
symbols.quote: The prefix moves and exchanges define the record permutation $L$ (neither a linear map, as on the contractions page, nor a dimension loss, as on the subspace-labels page); reversing them gives $L^{-1}$.

symbols.name: round input
symbols.meaning: The array entering a round of the transform.
symbols.quote: Truncation toward zero is odd and acts separately on each real and imaginary part, so for the array $z$ entering a round (not an address suffix, nor a binary vector of the phase-frames page) $J_EQ_p(\mathcal Hz)=Q_p(J_E\mathcal Hz)$: one truncation follows the exact round.

symbols.name: interchange exponent
symbols.meaning: The fixed exponent below 1 in the chunk interchange cost.
symbols.quote: $K$ is the chunk width in bits (not a tensor line or segment spacing); $\tau,\lambda'<1$ are the interchange and layer exponents.

symbols.name: layer exponent
symbols.meaning: The fixed exponent below 1 in the simultaneous layer cost.
symbols.quote: $K$ is the chunk width in bits (not a tensor line or segment spacing); $\tau,\lambda'<1$ are the interchange and layer exponents.
